question: Do highly accurate small transformers trained on decimal addition and subtraction share an exact, causally supported algorithm across seeds, lengths, and operations?

key_findings.claim: Rare carry and borrow cascades are the decisive data bottleneck for near-perfect arithmetic.
key_findings.evidence: After identifying failures on long cascades, the authors enrich an effectively infinite generator with those cases; 29 of 46 trained models exceed 99.999% accuracy on one million questions for lengths up to 13 digits.

key_findings.claim: Accurate models share a left-to-right progressive carry/borrow skeleton while implementation details vary.
key_findings.evidence: Automated node maps find the required BaseAdd/BaseDiff, immediate carry/borrow, resolved-cascade, sign, and operation roles with ordering constraints in every accurate model; heads, redundancy, timing, and routes differ.

key_findings.claim: Causal interventions close the earlier unresolved-carry gap only for a small worked subset.
key_findings.evidence: Activation and edge path patching show carry-specific delivery to answer combiners, and retaining mapped nodes preserves 0.89--0.94 of baseline in representative models; the deepest intervention battery covers four models while family-wide claims rely on automated maps and ablations.

key_findings.claim: Mixed-operation models reuse arithmetic circuitry polysemantically rather than simply allocating disjoint circuits.
key_findings.evidence: In a sample initialized mixed model, 88% of inserted addition nodes are reused for addition, 83% for positive subtraction, and 60% for negative subtraction; selection among co-computed results is distributed rather than rank-one.

key_findings.claim: The work does not show that the circuit transfers to frontier language models.
key_findings.evidence: All experiments use specialized roughly 10M-parameter, 2--3-layer models; the authors explicitly state that frontier LLMs can use hybrid circuits and make no transfer claim.

method.core_idea: Derive an exact symbolic arithmetic algorithm from model behavior, then test a declarative map of its subtask circuit with causal interventions.
method.mechanism: Train many small autoregressive transformers on edge-case-enriched equations, search attention/MLP nodes for predefined subtask signatures and temporal constraints, and validate nodes and edges with ablation, activation patching, path patching, interpolation, and sufficiency masks.
assumptions: The declarative subtask vocabulary contains the learned algorithm
Mean or resample ablations are faithful interventions
Linear probes recover relevant carry/borrow state
Specialized small models are a useful mechanistic testbed

techniques.role: Makes rare cascades common enough to learn and test.
Matches nodes to arithmetic subtasks under positional and causal constraints.
Tests delivery of resolved carry/borrow while controlling nuisance differences.
Checks whether the discovered node set actually preserves computation.

evaluations.setting: 46 addition, subtraction, or mixed models with 2--3 layers and lengths 5--15
evaluations.metric: accuracy on one million generated questions
evaluations.result: 29 models exceed 99.999%; inaccurate models lack parts of the proposed skeleton
evaluations.baseline: models trained without adequate rare-cascade mastery

evaluations.setting: four deeply studied models plus family-wide automated maps
evaluations.metric: patching effects, ablation accuracy, probe separation, constraint satisfaction
evaluations.result: causal support for carry/borrow delivery and 0.89--0.94 relative accuracy under representative sufficiency masks
evaluations.baseline: matched controls and random same-size node sets

limitations: Author-stated: deep causal evidence covers four worked examples.
Author-stated: larger-length carry sources are probe-limited.
Author-stated: redundant groups evade per-node attribution.
Author-stated: no transfer claim to frontier LLMs.
Reviewer inference: searching within a hand-designed subtask language can miss alternative but behaviorally equivalent algorithms.
failure_modes: A rare cascade absent from training yields apparently strong average accuracy but systematic failure.
Redundant nodes make single-component ablation falsely imply irrelevance.
A linear probe decodes information not used by the computation.
Mean ablation moves activations off distribution.
reusable_insights: Mine edge cases before attempting circuit interpretation of an almost-correct model.
Require circuit sufficiency in addition to feature decoding and necessity tests.
State invariants at the algorithm level separately from variable head-level implementations.
open_questions: Does the same skeleton emerge in larger pretrained models and other tokenizations?
Can automated discovery find subtasks without a hand-authored vocabulary?
How should causal confidence be calibrated under redundancy and superposition?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Addition in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Quirke and Barez explain one-layer n-digit addition and a rare high-loss case; this work covers deeper addition, subtraction, mixed operations, resolved cascades, and a 46-model family.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. reverse-engineer modular addition as a Fourier circuit and training-progress measure; this paper studies ordinary decimal carry/borrow algorithms and cross-model circuit families.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Circuit Analysis Interpretability Scale? Evidence from Multiple Choice Capabilities in Chinchilla
competitive_landscape.difference: Lieberum et al. apply circuit tools to a 70B model but obtain only a partial semantic explanation; this paper achieves an exact algorithmic account in tiny controlled models and explicitly leaves scale transfer open.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Accurate small arithmetic transformers share one exact circuit skeleton, including previously unresolved multi-digit carry and borrow mechanisms.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Family-wide maps and ablations plus detailed causal patching on four models support invariant subtasks with variable implementations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The calibrated distinction between algorithm invariance and implementation variability is strong and unusually testable. Universality beyond specialized small models remains an explicit open hypothesis.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete 18-page extraction and rechecked training, algorithms, family table, mixed-model results, causal interventions, and limitations. Three primary arXiv competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
